report.summary: Reviewed chunk 3 of daedalus/eval/harness.py: rows for arms aggregate, run_arms, _score, detect_provider, _ask, run_tier2, load_baseline, snapshot_baseline, write_baseline. Claims mostly kept; one uncheckable due to chunk boundary.
risks: _arms_aggregate | low | The n_c_beats_a and c_beats_a_ids counts are computed from rows already filtered as healthy by run_arms; if _arms_aggregate is reused with unfiltered rows, it could count errored rows. Current usage is safe; settle by confirming call sites.

run_tier2 | medium | The docstring says B's tokens were already measured with the real tokenizer, but the code measures tokens_B after truncation (count_tokens(ctx_b)) and separately reports tokens_B_true. The claim is about historical honesty, not current behavior, so it is not directly checkable.

run_tier2 | low | The OLLAMA_MODEL env var is read inside detect_provider, but the provider argument is normalized to lowercase; if a user passes a provider string like 'ollama' it is not handled specially, only 'none'/'off'/'deterministic' are. It falls through to probing, which is fine but the docstring does not mention 'ollama' as a keyword.
run_tier2 | medium | The docstring says B is capped at cap_tokens * 4 chars before being measured, and the code does cap_chars = cap_tokens * 4 and passes cap_chars to _whole_repo_text. This is kept.
snapshot_baseline | medium | Docstring says ERRORED tasks are skipped, and the comprehension filters on 'error' not in t and not t.get('focus_withheld'). This is kept.

write_baseline | low | The docstring says deterministic formatting (sorted keys), but the code only opens the file for writing; the JSON dump is not shown in this chunk, so the sorted-keys claim is uncheckable.

handoff.purpose: Arms aggregate, run_arms, Tier 2 scoring/provider/ask/run, baseline load/snapshot/write.

symbols.name: _arms_aggregate
symbols.note: Aggregates per-task arms rows: means, counts, and ids for c_beats_a and b_truncated_at_cap.

symbols.name: run_arms
symbols.note: Runs deterministic A/B/C comparison over tasks, skipping correctness tasks and collecting errors/focus-withheld; returns per-task, errored, and by-provenance aggregates.

symbols.name: _score
symbols.note: Checks whether all expected substrings appear case-insensitively; returns (all_present, fraction_present).

symbols.name: detect_provider
symbols.note: Probes local Ollama /api/tags with 2s timeout; returns provider descriptor or None; honors OLLAMA_HOST and OLLAMA_MODEL.

symbols.name: _ask
symbols.note: Single text-only chat completion against provider; never raises; returns empty string on any exception.

symbols.name: run_tier2
symbols.note: Opt-in LLM comparison of distilled slice vs whole-repo concat; skips cleanly if no provider; reports truncated B and true whole-repo token count.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_BASELINE_PATH
symbols.note: Path to baseline.json next to this file.

symbols.name: load_baseline
symbols.note: Reads baseline.json, or returns empty baseline if file does not exist.

symbols.name: snapshot_baseline
symbols.note: Builds baseline structure from current recall; skips errored and focus-withheld tasks; does not write disk.

symbols.name: write_baseline
symbols.note: Writes baseline JSON to path; docstring claims deterministic sorted keys but dump not shown in chunk.

claims.text: Tie-inclusive on purpose: a strict '>' here silently counted a BM25 tie as an A win ... with '>' the tie case ... was the ONLY case that could ever fire and it was being absorbed into 'no'.
claims.why: The code uses >=, which is tie-inclusive. The comment explains why strict > was wrong. This matches the code.

claims.text: Model-free (recall via _recall), offline, no LLM -- safe to run alongside Tier 1.
claims.why: run_arms only calls eval_task_arms, _correctness_task_row, _task_error_row, _repo_chunks, cached_index, resolve_task_repo; no provider or LLM calls are present in this chunk.

claims.text: See eval_task_arms for what each arm measures and by_provenance for the (never-blended) per-provenance-tier breakdown.
claims.why: eval_task_arms and _by_provenance are defined elsewhere in this file; this chunk cannot verify their behavior.

claims.text: Success = every expected substring appears (case-insensitive). Also return the fraction present for a softer signal.
claims.why: The code lowercases answer and each substring, checks presence, returns (present == len(answer_contains), present / len(answer_contains)).

claims.text: Only a local Ollama HTTP endpoint is probed (free, no key, no egress).
claims.why: The only network call is urllib.request.urlopen to host + '/api/tags' with timeout=2; no other egress in this function.

claims.text: The probe is a 2s GET to /api/tags -- it does nothing unless Tier 2 is requested.
claims.why: timeout=2 is used; detect_provider is only called from run_tier2 in this chunk.

claims.text: Single text-only turn against the provider. Never raises to the caller.
claims.why: The entire body is wrapped in try/except Exception; returns '' on any exception. The chat_completion call is inside the try.

claims.text: Opt-in Tier 2. Compares distilled-slice (A) vs whole-repo-concat (B) task success + tokens.
claims.why: The code computes ctx_a from semantic_slice and ctx_b from _whole_repo_text, asks both, and scores success and tokens.

claims.text: Cleanly skipped (never crashes) when no provider is up.
claims.why: If detect_provider returns None, run_tier2 returns a skipped dict immediately without further work.

claims.text: B's tokens were ALREADY measured with the real tokenizer before this change (count_tokens is exact whenever tiktoken is installed) -- that part was honest.
claims.why: This is a historical claim about prior behavior; the current code uses count_tokens(ctx_b) and count_tokens(full_text). The claim about 'before this change' cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: What was NOT honest: B is capped at cap_tokens * 4 chars before being measured, so tokens_B silently reflected a TRUNCATED text, not the real whole-repo size.
claims.why: The code sets cap_chars = cap_tokens * 4 and passes it to _whole_repo_text(repo, cap_chars); tokens_B is count_tokens(ctx_b) which is the truncated text. The 'NOT honest' refers to prior behavior, but the current code does cap B and reports tokens_B as the truncated count.

claims.text: tokens_B_true (added here) is the untruncated whole-repo token count, so a truncated B can never be mistaken for the real baseline.
claims.why: The code computes whole_true_tokens_cache[repo] = count_tokens(full_text) where full_text comes from _whole_repo_text(repo, cap_chars=None), and stores it as tokens_B_true in each row and in the aggregate.

claims.text: Same per-task resolution guard as Tier 1/arms: a bad repo label or an unindexed target must not take down an opt-in, potentially long-running LLM run over the rest of the task set.
claims.why: The try/except catches (ValueError, OSError) around resolve_task_repo, cached_index, _whole_repo_text, semantic_slice; on exception it appends an error row and continues.

claims.text: Read baseline.json, or an empty baseline if it does not exist yet (a fresh repo checkout before the first --update-baseline run).
claims.why: If os.path.exists(p) is False, returns {'schema': 1, 'tasks': {}}; otherwise opens and json.loads.

claims.text: Pure: build the baseline structure for the CURRENT recall of tasks (default TASKS). Does not touch disk -- see write_baseline.
claims.why: snapshot_baseline only calls run_tier1 and builds a dict; no file I/O appears in this function.

claims.text: Every task is snapshotted (including quarantine ones) so quarantine promotion is still comparable later; only PRIMARY tasks are ever gated (see run_gate).
claims.why: The code snapshots all tasks from run_tier1's per_task (excluding errored/focus_withheld), but the claim about gating only PRIMARY tasks depends on run_gate which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: ERRORED tasks (run_tier1) have no recall to snapshot and are skipped here -- they simply get no baseline entry, which makes them a 'new task' (not silently a pass) the next time run_gate sees them resolve successfully.
claims.why: The comprehension filters on 'error' not in t, so errored rows are excluded. The behavior of run_gate is not in this chunk, but the skipping is directly visible.

claims.text: FOCUS-WITHHELD tasks (the secret floor fail-closed on the task's own focus file) are skipped for the same reason: there is no recall key to snapshot, and re-baselining a fence-refused task would silently launder 'never measured' into 'passing'.
claims.why: The comprehension filters on not t.get('focus_withheld'), so such tasks are excluded. The reasoning about run_gate is not checkable here, but the exclusion is present.

claims.text: EXPLICIT-ONLY baseline write. Never call this from an automatic code path -- a baseline that updates itself is not a ratchet, it is a no-op.
claims.why: This is a policy claim about how the function should be used; the code itself does not enforce it. It cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: Deterministic formatting (sorted keys) so the diff is meaningful in review.
claims.why: The code opens the file but the json.dump call is cut off at the end of the chunk; the sort_keys argument is not visible.

observations.what: run_arms catches (ValueError, OSError) around repo resolution and indexing, but eval_task_arms is called outside the try block; however eval_task_arms is defined elsewhere and may raise uncaught exceptions.
detect_provider imports urllib.request inside the function; this is fine but unusual.
run_tier2 calls _whole_repo_text twice per repo: once with cap and once without. This may be inefficient but is not a correctness issue.

snapshot_baseline uses t['recall'] directly; if run_tier1 ever returns a row without 'recall' but without 'error' or 'focus_withheld', it would raise KeyError. The docstring claims only errored/focus_withheld lack recall, but this is not enforced in this chunk.
